w:r.w:t: App Structure, Dashboard Projection, Server-State Boundaries, Mutation Flows, Stale-State Handling, and UI Control Rules

This document defines the frontend architecture and state synchronization rules for Torgima Phase 1. It specifies how the Next.js frontend is organized, how screens read backend projections, how mutations are submitted, how stale state is detected, and how the UI remains a controlled execution environment instead of an independent source of truth.

The frontend is not only visual presentation. In Torgima, the UI guides execution, prevents invalid actions, reflects current system condition, and keeps the user focused on the next correct action. It must display validated state and never allow the user to act outside backend rules.
Rule: The frontend may display, request, and submit. It may not decide canonical state, generate tasks locally, approve proof, calculate condition, or override the Control Engine.
The frontend is a projection of system truth, not the owner of system truth.
Every screen must be built around the current backend projection. If frontend state is stale, the UI must refresh or block mutation rather than pretending its local view is current.

The frontend should make Torgima feel clear, alive, and controlled. It must reduce confusion, show the next correct action, and obey backend truth. The user should not feel the machinery, but the machinery must be present in every state, button, form, and refresh.
